topStories.headline: Midlothian Council Considers Digital Ranch Development Deal and Google-Site Power Request
topStories.dek: The October 13 City Council meeting took up a formal development agreement for the 873-acre Digital Ranch data campus and a zoning amendment that would allow on-site power generation at Google's existing Sharka district.
topStories.body:
Midlothian City Council met Tuesday, October 13, at 6 p.m. in the Council Chambers at City Hall to consider two significant data-center items that extend the city's position as one of North Texas's busiest industrial technology destinations.

The first item was a proposed development agreement with Digital Ranch LLC, listed as agenda item 2026-327. The council had unanimously approved, after a nearly 90-minute discussion at its September 22 meeting, a series of motions creating a planned development for a 395.7-acre portion of an 873.8-acre property on the city's southern end, and simultaneously establishing Midlothian Municipal Management District No. 4 to govern the acreage. The October 13 development agreement would set infrastructure obligations and binding conditions for that district. Digital Ranch is planning three data centers totaling 3.9 million square feet, four power-generating stations, and a closed-loop water system using no more than 0.5 million gallons per day, with setbacks requiring no building to be closer than 125 feet from a residential structure and noise capped at 60 decibels at the property line.

The second item was a zoning amendment for PD-106 — the 375.68-acre Sharka data center district along Railport Parkway, where Google has been building since 2019. A request filed August 10 asked the council to allow on-site power generation within that existing planned development. Google's newest building at the campus, dubbed Sharka Building 5, began construction in late January 2026 and is expected to complete by February 2027, representing an estimated $880 million investment in a 288,000-square-foot facility. Three earlier Sharka buildings are already operational.

Published minutes for the October 13 session had not been posted as of this edition's publication date. The city posts agendas, packets, and meeting videos at midlothian.tx.us.

topStories.headline: Early Voting Opens Monday as Midlothian Bond and Texas Midterm Head to the Polls
topStories.dek: Ellis County voters can cast ballots starting October 19 at any designated county location; Midlothian's five-proposition $192 million bond package appears alongside statewide and congressional races.
topStories.body:
Early voting begins Monday, October 19, and runs through Friday, October 30, with Election Day on Tuesday, November 3. Registered voters in Texas may cast their ballot at any designated early-voting location in the county where they are registered; hours vary by site, so residents should check the Ellis County elections office before heading out. The last day to apply for a ballot by mail is October 23 — applications must be received by the county clerk by that date, not merely postmarked.

For Midlothian voters, the November ballot carries five bond propositions the City Council approved unanimously earlier this year. Proposition A seeks $102.3 million for street and road improvements; Proposition B would fund a $6.8 million police substation; Proposition C covers $10 million in drainage improvements; Proposition D allocates $47.3 million to upgrade existing parks; and Proposition E provides $26.1 million to build new parks — a combined total of roughly $192 million.

The November 3 ballot also decides all 150 Texas House seats, 16 Texas Senate seats, all 38 U.S. House seats, and one U.S. Senate seat. Texas House District 10 covers all of Ellis County, including Waxahachie, Midlothian, Ennis, and Red Oak. The Dallas Morning News has published a North Texas voter guide at dallasnews.com covering local bond measures and candidate races.

topStories.headline: Midlothian Locks In YMCA Deal and School District Land for New Recreation Center with Competition Pool
topStories.dek: Agreements approved in September by both City Council and the MISD Board of Trustees formalize a 75-year ground lease and YMCA management pact for a facility that will include an indoor competition pool for the district's high school swim teams.
topStories.body:
Midlothian took a concrete step toward its long-planned community recreation center on September 22, when City Council approved two related agreements: a 75-year ground lease with Midlothian ISD for approximately five acres of district-owned land on South 14th Street at $1 per year, and a separate lease and operations agreement with the YMCA of Metropolitan Dallas to manage the finished facility.

The Midlothian ISD Board of Trustees approved the district's side of the arrangement at its September meeting, authorizing the long-term lease and shared-use agreement with the city. Under the deal, MISD will lease the land to allow the city to design and construct the center, and students will have access to the indoor competition pool for swim training and meets — giving the Midlothian High School and Heritage High School swim programs a local home pool for the first time.

The recreation center is funded through the city's voter-approved 2021 Bond Program and is planned for the block fronting the MISD Multi-Purpose Stadium on South 14th Street. Planned amenities include fitness and exercise spaces, gymnasium facilities, senior citizen exercise programs, indoor and outdoor pools, a splash pad, a child-watch center, a wellness center, and locker rooms. The YMCA of Metropolitan Dallas will handle day-to-day operations once the facility opens. A construction timeline has not yet been publicly announced.

moreNews.headline: Red Oak ISD Scores Gain on 2026 State Accountability Ratings
moreNews.body: Red Oak ISD posted a score of 78 on the 2026 Texas state accountability ratings, up from 77 the prior year, with the most notable gains in Student Achievement and School Progress scores. The ratings were released by the Texas Education Agency earlier this fall. The district's board holds its next regular meeting Monday, October 19, at 6 p.m. at the Education Service Center, 109 W. Red Oak Road.

moreNews.headline: MED and City Council Hold Special Joint Workshop on Economic Development
moreNews.body: The Midlothian Economic Development board listed an October 16, 2026 Special Called Joint Workshop on its public meeting calendar, bringing MED board members and the full City Council together to discuss economic development strategy and projects. A follow-up regular MED board meeting is scheduled for October 19. Agendas and any resulting documents will be posted at midlothian-tx.org.
